The SQL and Databases internship in short

In the SkillMe SQL and Databases internship you build one of 3 projects, such as ShelfWise: Library Management Database, a project where you design and query a database that tracks books, members and loans for a college library. In week 1 you create a small library database with books, members and loans tables, fill it with sample data and answer simple questions with SELECT. By week 4 you turn your database into a short analytics report that answers 8-10 real questions a librarian would ask. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

What you build

One of 3 real projects, built over four weeks

You are assigned one of these projects when you start, and build it milestone by milestone.

ShelfWise: Library Management Database

Design and query a database that tracks books, members and loans for a college library.

Week by week

What each week of the SQL and Databases internship covers

Shown for ShelfWise: Library Management Database. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Tables, Data and Your First Queries

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Create a small library database with books, members and loans tables, fill it with sample data and answer simple questions with SELECT. This is the foundation every later week builds on, so getting clean tables now saves time later.

    What you learn

    • What tables, rows, columns and data types are
    • Writing CREATE TABLE and INSERT statements
    • Filtering and sorting with SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY
    • Primary keys and why every row needs a unique id

    What you submit

    • schema.sql with three tables
    • seed.sql with sample data
    • queries_week1.sql with 8 commented queries
    • README with a screenshot of the tables in DB Browser
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • Running schema.sql then seed.sql on an empty database finishes with no errors
    • Each table has a primary key
    • The database contains at least 20 books, 10 members and 25 loans
    • All 8 queries run and return the expected rows

    Stretch goal: Add a genres column and write a query that lists all books in one genre sorted by publication year.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Relationships, JOINs and Grouping

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Connect your tables with foreign keys and use JOINs and GROUP BY to answer questions that span several tables. You will also tidy the design so data is not repeated.

    What you learn

    • Foreign keys and constraints such as NOT NULL, UNIQUE and CHECK
    • INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN
    • Aggregates with GROUP BY and HAVING
    • Basic normalisation: removing repeated data into its own table

    What you submit

    • Updated schema.sql with foreign keys and constraints
    • queries_week2.sql with at least 9 JOIN and GROUP BY queries
    • Screenshot showing a constraint rejecting bad data
    • README section on normalisation
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • An authors table exists and books references it by id
    • Inserting a loan with an invalid member id fails with a foreign key error
    • At least one query uses LEFT JOIN to find unmatched rows
    • At least one query uses HAVING correctly
    • All scripts still run cleanly on an empty database

    Stretch goal: Support books with multiple authors by adding a book_authors linking table and query it with two JOINs.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Subqueries, Views and Indexes

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Answer harder questions with subqueries and CTEs, save useful queries as views, and make lookups faster with indexes. You will also learn to read a simple query plan.

    What you learn

    • Subqueries and Common Table Expressions (WITH)
    • Creating and using views
    • What an index is and when it helps
    • Reading EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN output at a basic level

    What you submit

    • queries_week3.sql with subqueries and at least one CTE
    • views.sql with two views
    • indexes.sql with at least one index
    • README section with before/after query plan screenshots
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • At least 3 queries use a subquery and at least 1 uses a CTE
    • Both views exist and return correct rows
    • EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN output changes from SCAN to SEARCH after adding the index
    • The database has at least 200 loans

    Stretch goal: Use a window function like RANK() to rank members by number of loans within each month.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    Library Insights Report

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Turn your database into a short analytics report that answers 8-10 real questions a librarian would ask. Finish with an ER diagram, a clean README and a demo.

    What you learn

    • Framing business questions and answering them with SQL
    • Drawing an ER diagram
    • Presenting query results clearly
    • Optionally connecting SQL to a simple front-end

    What you submit

    • report.sql answering 8-10 questions
    • REPORT.md with results and insights
    • ER diagram image
    • Demo video or screenshots, plus an optional Streamlit app
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • The report answers at least 8 distinct questions, each with a working query
    • Each answer includes a one-line plain-English insight
    • The ER diagram matches the actual tables and relationships
    • Someone can rebuild the database from the README instructions alone

    Stretch goal: Add a fines table and a query that calculates the total fine each member owes for overdue books.

SQL and Databases internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the SQL and Databases internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: ShelfWise: Library Management Database, ShopLens: E-commerce Sales Analytics or StatsPitch: Cricket Stats Database. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the SQL and Databases internship?

The SQL and Databases internship works with SQL, PostgreSQL and Data Modeling. Week 1: what tables, rows, columns and data types are; writing CREATE TABLE and INSERT statements. Week 2: foreign keys and constraints such as NOT NULL, UNIQUE and CHECK; INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN. Week 3: subqueries and Common Table Expressions (WITH); creating and using views. Week 4: framing business questions and answering them with SQL; drawing an ER diagram.

Do I need experience to apply for the SQL and Databases internship?

You need the basics of SQL, PostgreSQL and Data Modeling, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you create a small library database with books, members and loans tables, fill it with sample data and answer simple questions with SELECT. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each SQL and Databases milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of ShelfWise: Library Management Database, that means: running schema.sql then seed.sql on an empty database finishes with no errors; each table has a primary key; the database contains at least 20 books, 10 members and 25 loans; all 8 queries run and return the expected rows. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the SQL and Databases internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Designed a three-table library database in SQLite; Wrote CREATE and INSERT scripts to build and seed the database from scratch; Answered 8 practical questions using SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY; Normalised a library database and linked tables with foreign keys; Added constraints that block invalid data at the database level; Wrote JOIN and GROUP BY queries to find popular books and active members; Wrote subqueries and CTEs to answer multi-step questions about library usage; Created views to simplify common reports; Added an index and verified the speed-up with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN; Built an analytics report answering 10 library questions with SQL; Documented the schema with an ER diagram and reproducible build scripts; Shared insights on borrowing trends from my own library database.

What are the other projects in the SQL and Databases internship?

ShopLens: E-commerce Sales Analytics: Build a small online-store database and use SQL to find out what sells, who buys and when. StatsPitch: Cricket Stats Database: Load real cricket match data into a database and use SQL to uncover player and team stats. Every project follows the same four-week shape, with one reviewed milestone a week.

Is the SQL and Databases internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based and goes to the interns whose reviewed SQL and Databases work stands out in their cohort, not to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
